Package org.checkerframework.framework.stub

Class BinaryStubData

java.lang.Object
org.checkerframework.framework.stub.BinaryStubData
public class BinaryStubData extends Object
In-memory representation of a binary stub file: the annotated JDK (annotated-jdk.bin.gz) or the binary form of a built-in checker stub file (*.astub.bin.gz). The binary format stores annotation information extracted from the stub sources in a compact, pre-parsed form that is faster to load than the original text stubs.

Instances are immutable after construction and contain no javac objects (only strings and primitives), so they are cached per JVM and shared across compilations; see AnnotationFileElementTypes#loadedBinaryStubData.

The binary format consists of a GZIP-compressed stream containing:

  1. A 4-byte magic number (0xCF4A444B).
  2. A 2-byte version number.
  3. A source fingerprint: a 4-byte source length (-1 if none was recorded, as for the annotated JDK and other stub files generated by JavaStubifier), followed, when non-negative, by the 32-byte SHA-256 digest of the source .astub file's raw bytes. Used only to detect a stale binary for a user-supplied -Astubs file; see matchesSource(byte[]).
  4. A constant pool of UTF-8 strings (class names, field names, signatures, string literals).
  5. An annotation pool of structural annotation records.
  6. A sequence of BinaryStubData.ClassRecord entries, one per class, interface, enum, annotation type, or record.
  7. Package and module annotation records.

    • CF_COMMENT

      public static final String CF_COMMENT
      Fully-qualified name of CFComment, which is never written to the binary format. Defined once in BinaryStubWriter.CF_COMMENT.

      Re-exported here so that BinaryStubDiffChecker, which must filter the same annotation out of the text-parsed side, can name it without depending on the stubifier source set: framework-test, where that class lives, does not have the stubifier on its classpath. This is a compile-time constant, so reading it creates no runtime dependency.

      See Also:
      • Constant Field Values

    • stringPool

      public final String[] stringPool
      All strings referenced by the binary data.

      These are not interned. Nothing compares them by reference: class names and signatures are only ever used as map keys or compared with equals, and the one identity comparison on an annotation name (BinaryStubReader.isAnnotatedForThisChecker) compares the result of AnnotationUtils.annotationName, which is interned by its own contract, not a string from this pool.

      Interning them bought nothing and cost most of the load: interning this pool's ~24,000 strings took the annotated JDK's binary stub file from about 20 ms to about 130 ms to load (measured; the cost is the cold string-table insertions). That is once per JVM, since the parsed data is cached in AnnotationFileElementTypes#loadedBinaryStubData.

  • Constructor Details

    • BinaryStubData

      public BinaryStubData(InputStream in) throws IOException
      Reads binary stub data from the given stream. The stream must supply the GZIP-compressed binary format written by BinaryStubWriter. Prefer read(java.io.InputStream), which additionally reports a damaged file's out-of-range pool index as an IOException.
      Parameters:
      in - the input stream to read from; the stream is closed when this constructor returns
      Throws:
      IOException - if the stream cannot be read or contains an invalid/unsupported format

  • Method Details

    • read

      public static BinaryStubData read(InputStream in) throws IOException
      Reads binary stub data from the given stream, reporting a damaged file as an IOException regardless of how the damage surfaces. A damaged file can hold an index that points outside a pool, which this class does not validate (unlike a count; see readCount(java.io.DataInputStream, java.lang.String)) and which surfaces as ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException; converting it lets the caller fall back to text parsing instead of crashing the compilation.
      Parameters:
      in - the input stream to read from; the stream is closed when this method returns
      Returns:
      the binary stub data read from in
      Throws:
      IOException - if the stream cannot be read or contains an invalid/unsupported format

    • matchesSource

      public boolean matchesSource(byte[] sourceBytes)

      Parameters:

      Returns:
      true if sourceBytes matches the fingerprint this binary was generated from
